tools.name: bulk_grade_submissions
tools.description:
Grade multiple submissions efficiently with concurrent processing.

Supports both rubric-based and simple point-based grading in batches.
Each target is read before a single write and inspected afterward.
Results retain prose and append versioned recovery JSON identifying
verified, rejected, unknown, and unattempted targets. Authorization
failures stop later batches; already dispatched writes cannot be undone.
Comments append, so unknown comment outcomes must be inspected before retry.

parameters.name: grades
parameters.description:
Dict mapping user_id to {rubric_assessment?, grade?, comment?, expected_attempt?}.
expected_attempt binds the write to the reviewed attempt; null
requires an explicitly never-submitted baseline.
OMIT `comment` unless the instructor explicitly asked for written
feedback. "Assign grade 8" means the grade ONLY. A comment is
visible to the student in SpeedGrader, APPENDS a new comment on
every call rather than replacing the previous one, and cannot be
un-sent. Never generate a comment that merely restates the grade
or narrates that grading happened.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: If True, validate without submitting (default: False)

tools.returns: Summary of grading: total, successful, failed, error details
examples: Grade these 10 students with their specific rubric scores
tools.notes: Use dry_run=true first to preview. For complex grading logic, consider execute_typescript instead.

Unpublish these five pages

tools.name: capture_record_snapshot
tools.returns: Tool result; Canvas-authored content is marked as untrusted data
tools.description:
Preview then capture a private educator record snapshot using Canvas GETs only.

Confirm identical arguments after reviewing the local storage scope.
Each call reads at most page_budget record pages (1..100), plus course,
permission and caller checks. Resume an interrupted/partial directory
with the original scope and a fresh preview. Names, content and comments
are excluded by default. Attachment IDs/size/type may be explicitly
included for a separate bounded download. Bytes, Inbox and discussions
are excluded from this capture.
Numeric IDs remain identifying; summaries contain no student records.
This is scoped evidence, not a transaction or a restoration operation.

tools.name: check_enrollment
tools.description:
Check whether a specific campus login ID is enrolled in a course.

Answers a roster-membership question about an externally-supplied person
(NOT the caller). Returns only a yes/no plus minimal enrollment metadata —
never the roster, names, or grades. Requires a Canvas token with
roster-admin rights; without them the answer is INDETERMINATE, never "no".

To ask about YOURSELF, use get_my_enrollments instead — it needs no
roster permission and cannot return an indeterminate answer.

Note that `role` defaults to "student". A NO answer is scoped to that
role and will name any other role the person holds; pass role="any" when
you just want to know whether they are in the course at all.

parameters.name: course_identifier
parameters.description: Course code, numeric ID, or SIS ID.

parameters.name: net_id
parameters.description:
The person's campus login ID — NetID, uniqname, campus ID, or
  the full email-style Canvas login. Matched against Canvas
  `login_id` then `sis_user_id`; `jdoe` and `jdoe@example.edu`
  are treated as the same identifier. Not a display name.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description:
Enrollment type that satisfies the check — "student" (default),
  "teacher", "ta", "observer", "designer", or "any".

tools.returns: Yes/no plus minimal enrollment metadata (state, role, matched field) — never the roster
tools.notes: Data-minimizing roster-membership check for external access gating. Requires a teacher-scoped token; a student token yields a clean Canvas 403.

tools.name: create_rubric

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: JSON string defining rubric criteria (schema and example in the tool description)

parameters.name: assignment_id
parameters.description: Optional assignment ID to immediately associate the rubric with

parameters.name: use_for_grading
parameters.description:
When associating with an assignment, use rubric for grade
             calculation (default: False)

parameters.name: reusable
parameters.description: Make rubric reusable across courses (default: False)

parameters.name: free_form_criterion_comments
parameters.description:
Allow free-form comments per criterion
                          instead of rating selection (default: False)

tools.returns: Created rubric details including ID, points, and any assignment association
examples: Create a 20-point rubric with criteria for clarity and analysis
tools.notes: Uses bracket-notation form-data encoding required by the Canvas rubric API. The ``criteria`` parameter is a JSON string mapping arbitrary criterion keys to objects with the following fields: - ``description`` (required): Short criterion label shown in the rubric grid - ``points`` (required): Maximum points for this criterion (non-negative number) - ``long_description`` (optional): Detailed criterion description - ``ratings`` (optional): List (or object) of rating levels, each with:     - ``description`` (required): Rating label (e.g. "Excellent")     - ``points`` (required): Points for this rating (non-negative number)     - ``long_description`` (optional): Detailed rating description Example ``criteria`` JSON:: {       "c1": {         "description": "Content Quality",         "points": 10,         "ratings": [           {"description": "Excellent", "points": 10},           {"description": "Satisfactory", "points": 7},           {"description": "Needs Work", "points": 3}         ]       },       "c2": {         "description": "Grammar",         "points": 5,         "ratings": [           {"description": "No errors", "points": 5},           {"description": "Minor errors", "points": 3}         ]       }     }

tools.name: create_rubric_from_csv
tools.description:
Create one or more rubrics in a course from a CSV string.

Uses Canvas's native rubric CSV import endpoint, then polls the import
job until it reaches a terminal workflow_state.

A ``Rubric Name`` column is REQUIRED — Canvas rejects the import without
it and creates nothing. Required format (repeat the rating triple per
rating level; a distinct Rubric Name per row creates multiple rubrics)::

    Rubric Name,Criteria Name,Criteria Description,Criteria Enable Range,Rating Name,Rating Description,Rating Points
    Essay Rubric,Clarity,Is the argument clear,false,Excellent,Very clear,10

Two Canvas behaviours to be aware of:

- Imported rubrics land in the ``Draft`` state and are **not** returned
  by ``list_rubrics`` / ``GET /courses/:id/rubrics``, though they do
  appear on the course Rubrics page. An empty ``list_rubrics`` result is
  not evidence the import failed.
- ``succeeded_with_errors`` is a terminal state, not a transient one, and
  can mean zero rubrics were created.

parameters.name: csv_content
parameters.description: The content of the CSV file as a string

tools.returns: Import status with created rubric names/IDs, or per-row errors if the import partially failed
examples: Import these three rubrics from CSV
tools.notes: Uses Canvas's native rubric CSV import endpoint, then polls the import job until it reaches a terminal workflow_state. A ``Rubric Name`` column is REQUIRED — Canvas rejects the import without it and creates nothing. Required format (repeat the rating triple per rating level; a distinct Rubric Name per row creates multiple rubrics):: Rubric Name,Criteria Name,Criteria Description,Criteria Enable Range,Rating Name,Rating Description,Rating Points     Essay Rubric,Clarity,Is the argument clear,false,Excellent,Very clear,10 Two Canvas behaviours to be aware of: - Imported rubrics land in the ``Draft`` state and are **not** returned   by ``list_rubrics`` / ``GET /courses/:id/rubrics``, though they do   appear on the course Rubrics page. An empty ``list_rubrics`` result is   not evidence the import failed. - ``succeeded_with_errors`` is a terminal state, not a transient one, and   can mean zero rubrics were created.

afterwards; in container mode it is streamed to the sandboxed process

Submit one of YOUR OWN assignments. Consumes an attempt.

Two-step by design. Call it without a confirmation_token to get a
preview of exactly what would be sent plus a token; show that preview
to the student, and only after they approve it call again passing the
token to actually submit.
The token expires, is single-use, and is void if the content or the
attempt count changed since the preview.

parameters.name: file_paths
parameters.description: Local file paths (local stdio servers only, any file type)

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: Optional comment to include with the submission

parameters.name: confirmation_token
parameters.description: Token from the preview call; omit to preview

tools.returns: A preview plus confirmation token on the first call; the submission result on the second
examples: Submit my essay to assignment 4821
Yes, submit it
tools.notes: Disabled unless the operator lists it in STUDENT_WRITE_TOOLS, and an instructor can block it per course. Group assignments and quizzes are not supported.

tools.name: update_rubric
tools.description:
Safely replace an existing rubric after preview and confirmation.

Canvas updates replace the full criteria set. ``criteria`` must
therefore be an ID-keyed JSON object containing every current criterion
and rating, with each object's ``id`` repeated inside it. This tool does
not add or remove criteria/ratings; it edits their text and points while
preserving IDs used by existing assessments.

Call once without ``confirmation_token`` to receive a preview, show it
to the educator, and only after they approve it call again with
identical arguments and the token.
Any rubric or association drift invalidates the token.

Omit ``free_form_criterion_comments`` to preserve the rubric's current
setting, or pass a boolean to change it explicitly.

parameters.name: rubric_association_id
parameters.description:
The rubric's association ID for the course
or assignment, shown as "Rubric Association ID" by get_rubric

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Rubric title (pass the current title to keep it)

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description:
JSON object keyed by existing criterion ID; each value
repeats its "id" and carries description, points, optional
long_description, and a ratings object keyed by existing rating
ID in the same shape. Every current criterion and rating must be
present

parameters.name: free_form_criterion_comments
parameters.description:
True/False to change the setting;
omit to keep the current one

parameters.name: confirmation_token
parameters.description: Token from the preview call; omit to preview

tools.returns: A no-write preview with confirmation token, or a verified update result
examples: Preview an ID-preserving update to rubric 7371 and association 8801
tools.notes: Two-step destructive tool. It fetches the complete rubric and association, rejects missing or unknown criterion/rating IDs, preserves non-editable scoring flags, binds the preview token to current and requested state, and re-reads the rubric after the PUT. A different returned rubric ID or association ID is reported as unconfirmed and is never retried automatically.

tools.name: update_syllabus
tools.description:
Set the Canvas Syllabus tab content for a course.

Canvas keeps no revision history for the syllabus, so replacing a
syllabus that already has content is a two-step call: call without
confirmation_token to get a preview plus a single-use token, show the
preview to the educator, and only after they approve it call again with
the token and identical arguments. Writing into an empty syllabus, or appending/prepending,
destroys nothing and takes a single call.

parameters.name: syllabus_body
parameters.description:
HTML for the syllabus. Canvas stores this as HTML;
plain text is accepted but renders without formatting.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description:
"replace" (default) swaps the whole body, "append" adds to
the end of the existing body, "prepend" adds to the start.

parameters.name: confirmation_token
parameters.description:
Token from the preview call. Only needed when
replacing a syllabus that already has content; a token that is
supplied is always checked, in every mode.

tools.returns: Confirmation that the syllabus was written, verified by reading it back from Canvas. Replacing existing content first returns a preview plus a single-use token and writes nothing.
examples: Add a link to the course website at the top of the BADM 350 syllabus
Replace the CS101 syllabus with this HTML
tools.notes: Canvas keeps no revision history for syllabus_body, so a replace cannot be undone. Append and prepend, and any write into an empty syllabus, are single-call because they destroy nothing.
